works.version_read: Author manuscript dated 28 January 2019, 29 pages; final ISQ article pagination is not used for manuscript claims
works.coverage: All 29 pages including notes and references; figures on pp.17 and 19 visually inspected. Final typeset article, supplementary files and replication data not inspected.
works.method: Two online survey experiments in China, October 2015–March 2016; samples 2,992 and 5,445. Voluntary online panels, not random national samples.
limits: Threat-specificity comparison spans different scenarios, with a finality confound discussed on manuscript p.20.
Several plotted effects are not statistically distinguishable from zero at the 5% level; manuscript p.22 acknowledges small, incompletely robust effects.
Public approval experiments cannot establish actual leaders' beliefs, negotiating mandates or crisis concessions.

works.version_read: Complete publisher HTML, Foreign Policy Analysis 18(3), orac012
works.coverage: Complete main text, footnotes, references and tables; all eight figures visually inspected. No PDF page citations claimed. Underlying corpus/coding not replicated.
works.method: Comparison of selected foreign-policy passages in Chinese/English statement pairs; interpretive coding of differences and signaled intentions.
limits: Table 3's inference from textual differences to challenges to existing rules requires independent contextual evaluation.
Footnote 4: eleven of twelve substantive differences in 2019 concentrated in two documents; one lacked a complete English translation.
The study leaves motives for translation differences unresolved. Do not infer deliberate deception, policy contradiction, or a new negotiating style from omission alone.
Reported corpus is 91 documents; displayed Table 1 category counts sum to 96. Denominator discrepancy not resolved or used for our own numerical claims.
